dataset.source: EARS subset already staged at data/datasets/ears-blind/audio

pilot_evidence.interpretation: On the frozen synthetic pilot the postfilter adds 0.282 dB SI-SDR to the 4-bit stress proxy and removes 4.873 dB from the 8-bit proxy, while STOI is effectively unchanged. The effect is small, sign-dependent and limited to a non-standard proxy.
limitations: These are controlled synthetic degradations, not a real-capture restoration benchmark.
No human listening test or listener quality score was run.
The tested classical methods are reference baselines, not faithful reproductions of SPADE, NU-Wave 2, Opus 1.5 neural features, or a universal neural restorer.
Codec modeling isolates 8-bit mu-law and a 4-bit mu-law proxy at 8 kHz; the 4-bit case is not a standard codec. Neither models MP3/AAC/Opus transform artifacts, tandem coding, or network jitter.
Packet masks are known to the restoration methods, an easier condition than blind packet-loss detection.

No ML model was evaluated because the locally available ROSE-CD checkpoint targets additive-noise/reverberation enhancement, while the task-specific NU-Wave 2 and Opus neural restoration runtimes/checkpoints are not staged here.

source_evidence_statements: research/distortion_restoration_20261028.md records four separate restoration tasks and states that the 4-bit mu-law case is a stress proxy, not a standard codec, and that neither proxy models MP3/AAC/Opus transform artifacts, tandem coding or jitter.

scripts/evaluate_distortion_restoration.py builds the narrowband reference with 16 kHz -> 8 kHz resample_poly, applies the proxy, upsamples 8 kHz -> 16 kHz and postfilters at 3900 Hz with butter(4) + sosfiltfilt.
The frozen report aggregate for RST-03 records +0.282 dB SI-SDR for the 4-bit proxy and -4.873 dB for the 8-bit proxy, with STOI effectively unchanged; these are provenance values only.
